preconditions.description: The input s must be either a string or an integer.

postconditions.description: The function always returns a string.
If the input is an integer, the output is the string representation of that integer.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(s, str) and all(c.islower() or c.isdigit() or c == '_' for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: If the input is a string, the output contains only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(s, str) and return_value.count('_') == sum(1 for i in range(1, len(s)) if s[i].isupper())
postconditions.description: If the input is a string, the number of underscores in the output equals the number of uppercase letters in the input that are not at the start of the string.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(s, str) and return_value.replace('_', '') == ''.join(c.lower() if c.isalpha() else c for c in s)
postconditions.description: If the input is a string, removing underscores from the output yields the input string with all alphabetic characters lowercased.
